hypothesis: A hash-bound v14-to-v21 transition can preserve every active v14 lifecycle until a completed drain, then start the exact evidence-routed portfolio with retest v2 observation but no retest execution authority.
decision: Keep v21 inactive and bind its future transition to the machine-tested runbook. Require the exact v14 identity, completed transition drain, all assets flat, no owned orders, recoverable archive, report-only v21 reconciliation, exact v21 profile and source hashes, a fresh verified pre-start backup, and new explicit live approval. This revision records a reproducible path; it does not request or initiate the drain and does not alter the active v14 process.
falsifier: The transition contract is falsified by any mismatch in current or candidate profile bytes, fingerprints, v1/v2/ETH source hashes, executable routes, retest observe-only scope, flat/order-free state, completed drain, or backup identity. Mechanical correctness does not establish economic edge and must not be interpreted as a profitability claim.
limitations: The transition has not occurred and is not authorized by this record.
BTC, ETH, and SOL remain active v14 lifecycles at the time of preparation, so the flat-boundary predicates are not satisfied.
The runbook validates mechanics and traceability, not profitability or route expectancy.
A future start requires fresh runtime and venue evidence; passing static tests cannot substitute for flat/order-free reconciliation.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, sizing policy, backend process, checkpoint process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
